title: Découvrir les sons autour de nous
oneGoal: Students will identify and distinguish between different sounds in their environment using their sense of hearing
decisionPoints: Are students comfortable closing their eyes to focus on listening?
Should we start with obvious loud sounds or subtle quiet sounds?
Do students need visual cues to support sound identification?
progression: Foundation lesson - introduces sound as a scientific concept and builds listening awareness
realWorldConnection: Understanding how we use hearing to stay safe and enjoy music, like hearing car horns or birds singing

title: Sons forts et sons doux
oneGoal: Students will compare and contrast loud sounds and soft sounds using descriptive vocabulary
decisionPoints: Which classroom sounds demonstrate loud/soft contrast most clearly?
Should we use musical instruments or everyday objects for sound comparison?
Are students ready for volume control activities or should we focus on recognition?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by adding vocabulary and classification skills to sound observation
realWorldConnection: Learning to adjust our voices for different situations, like whispering in libraries or calling friends outside

title: Sons aigus et sons graves
oneGoal: Students will distinguish between high-pitched and low-pitched sounds through listening activities
decisionPoints: Which pitch examples are most obvious and engaging for Grade 1 students?
Should we use voices, instruments, or both to demonstrate pitch differences?
Are students ready for pitch matching activities or should we focus on identification?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by introducing pitch as another way to describe and classify sounds
realWorldConnection: Recognizing different voices (mom's low voice, baby's high voice) and animal sounds (bird tweets, cow moos)

title: D'où viennent les sons?
oneGoal: Students will identify that sounds come from vibrating objects and sources around them
decisionPoints: What objects provide clear, visible vibration examples for young students?
Should we start with large, obvious vibrations or focus on discovering hidden sources?
Are students ready to feel vibrations safely or should we focus on visual observation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by connecting sound perception to physical cause - vibration
realWorldConnection: Understanding that speakers vibrate to make music and our throat vibrates when we talk

title: Sentir les vibrations
oneGoal: Students will safely feel vibrations while sounds are being produced using hands-on exploration
decisionPoints: Which safe vibration activities provide the clearest tactile experience?
Should students explore individual vibrating objects or work with partners?
Are students ready for guided discovery or need structured demonstrations?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by adding tactile experience to connect feeling vibrations with hearing sounds
realWorldConnection: Feeling the vibrations in a guitar or piano when someone plays, or feeling our chest when we sing loudly

title: Fabriquer un téléphone à ficelle
oneGoal: Students will construct and test a simple string telephone to explore how sound travels
decisionPoints: What cup and string materials work best for clear sound transmission?
Should students work in pairs or small groups for telephone construction?
Are students ready for independent testing or need guided exploration steps?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by introducing sound transmission and hands-on construction of sound devices
realWorldConnection: Understanding how phones and communication devices help us talk to people far away

title: Explorer les tambours
oneGoal: Students will investigate how different sizes and materials affect drum sounds through experimentation
decisionPoints: Which container sizes and materials provide the most interesting sound contrasts?
Should students experiment freely or follow structured comparison activities?
Are students ready for rhythm creation or should we focus on sound exploration?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by focusing on percussion instruments and how physical properties affect sound
realWorldConnection: Connecting to music and rhythm in different cultures, like drums in celebrations and parades

title: Construire un kazoo
oneGoal: Students will create a kazoo instrument and explore how their voice creates vibrations and sound
decisionPoints: What materials create the most satisfying kazoo sound experience?
Should students personalize their kazoos or focus on consistent construction?
Are students ready for solo performances or should we start with group humming?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by connecting voice production to instrument making and vibration concepts
realWorldConnection: Understanding how musical instruments help us make music and express ourselves creatively

title: Bouteilles musicales
oneGoal: Students will create musical bottles with different water levels to produce different pitches
decisionPoints: How many water levels create clear pitch differences without overwhelming students?
Should students blow across bottles or tap them for sound production?
Are students ready for creating simple melodies or should we focus on pitch exploration?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by demonstrating how changing physical properties (water level) changes pitch
realWorldConnection: Connecting to how different sized instruments make different sounds, like piccolo vs. tuba

title: Maracas et shakers
oneGoal: Students will construct shaker instruments using various materials to explore how contents affect sound quality
decisionPoints: Which filling materials provide interesting sound contrasts (rice, beans, pebbles)?
Should students test different amounts of filling or different container sizes?
Are students ready for creating rhythm patterns or should we focus on sound comparison?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by exploring how different materials and amounts create different sound qualities
realWorldConnection: Understanding rhythm instruments in music and how different materials make different sounds in daily life

title: Guitare en boîte
oneGoal: Students will build a simple box guitar with rubber bands to explore string vibrations and pitch
decisionPoints: Which box sizes and rubber band tensions create the clearest sound differences?
Should students use different rubber band thicknesses or focus on tension changes?
Are students ready for finger picking or should we use picks for string plucking?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by introducing string instruments and how tension affects pitch
realWorldConnection: Connecting to real guitars, violins, and other string instruments in music and how they work

title: Flûte de Pan avec pailles
oneGoal: Students will create a panpipe instrument using straws to demonstrate how length affects pitch
decisionPoints: How many different straw lengths provide clear pitch progression without complexity?
Should students cut their own straws or use pre-cut lengths for consistency?
Are students ready for playing simple tunes or should we focus on pitch sequence understanding?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by introducing wind instruments and how length affects pitch in air columns
realWorldConnection: Understanding how flutes, recorders, and organ pipes work by changing air column length

title: Orchestre de la classe
oneGoal: Students will combine all their handmade instruments to create a class orchestra and perform together
decisionPoints: Should we assign specific instrument roles or let students choose their favorites?
What simple songs or rhythms work best for showcasing different instrument types?
Are students ready for conducting signals or should we focus on playing together?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by combining all instrument knowledge into collaborative music making
realWorldConnection: Understanding how orchestras and bands work together to create beautiful music performances

title: Concert de démonstration
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate their understanding of sound and vibration by performing and explaining their instruments
decisionPoints: Should students present individually, in pairs, or as small ensembles?
What audience (other classes, parents, or school community) would be most supportive?
Are students ready for explaining how their instruments work or should we focus on performance?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by culminating unit learning through performance and scientific explanation
realWorldConnection: Understanding that musicians share their music with others and can explain how their instruments work

title: Sons dans la nature
oneGoal: Students will apply their sound knowledge to identify and classify natural sounds during outdoor exploration (extension)
decisionPoints: Which outdoor locations provide the richest variety of natural sounds for exploration?
Should students record sounds using technology or focus on careful listening and description?
Are students ready for independent sound hunting or need guided group exploration?
progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - applies sound classification skills to natural environment exploration
realWorldConnection: Understanding how animals, wind, and water create sounds in nature and how we can enjoy natural music

title: Échos et réflexion du son
oneGoal: Students will explore how sounds bounce back to create echoes in different environments (extension)
decisionPoints: Which school locations provide safe, clear echo experiences for young students?
Should we use voice calls, clapping, or instrument sounds for echo exploration?
Are students ready for understanding sound reflection or should we focus on experiencing echoes?
progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - introduces sound reflection as an advanced concept through playful exploration
realWorldConnection: Understanding echoes in tunnels, mountains, and large buildings, and how some animals use echoes to navigate

title: Musique du monde
oneGoal: Students will explore instruments and musical sounds from different cultures around the world (extension)
decisionPoints: Which cultural instruments are accessible for student exploration and culturally appropriate to share?
Should we focus on listening to recordings or hands-on exploration of cultural instruments?
Are students ready for discussing cultural connections or should we focus on sound exploration?
progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - expands sound knowledge to include cultural diversity in music and instruments
realWorldConnection: Understanding that people around the world create music with different instruments and traditions

title: Inventions sonores créatives
oneGoal: Students will design and create their own original sound-making device using recycled materials (extension)
decisionPoints: What recycled materials are safe and offer good potential for creative sound making?
Should students work individually on inventions or collaborate in small teams?
Are students ready for independent design or need guided brainstorming and planning?
progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - applies all sound knowledge to original creative invention and design thinking
realWorldConnection: Understanding that inventors and musicians create new instruments and that we can be creative problem solvers

title: Enregistrer nos créations
oneGoal: Students will record their musical creations and listen back to evaluate their sound productions (extension)
decisionPoints: What recording technology is available and appropriate for Grade 1 students to use?
Should students record individual performances or group collaborations?
Are students ready for self-evaluation of their recordings or need guided listening support?
progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - introduces technology for documenting and reflecting on musical learning
realWorldConnection: Understanding how musicians record music and how we can use technology to save and share our creative work

title: Festival des sons et vibrations
oneGoal: Students will organize and participate in a celebration showcasing all their sound and music learning (extension)
decisionPoints: What festival format allows all students to showcase their learning and feel successful?
Should the festival include performances, demonstrations, or interactive sound stations?
How can families and community members be invited to celebrate student learning?
progression: Extension of Lesson 19 - culminates entire unit with community celebration and sharing of all sound learning
realWorldConnection: Understanding that communities celebrate music and learning together, and that we can share our knowledge with others
